# Ontario Landlord Document-Prep Checklist

For a month-to-month tenancy in Ontario, the safest path is to document the unpaid rent and damage carefully, use the correct LTB forms, and avoid self-help steps like changing locks or shutting off services.

## Eviction Path, Evidence, and Timing

| Step | What to do | Key details | Timing note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm rent ledger | Record the monthly rent of **CAD 1,850**, due dates, payments received, arrears total, and any NSF fees if applicable | Do this before serving any notice |
| 2 | Document damage | Photograph/video each item, date-stamp files, and keep repair quotes/invoices | Capture condition before repairs if possible |
| 3 | Serve rent arrears notice | Use the Ontario LTB notice for non-payment of rent, commonly **N4** | The notice must give the tenant a legal period to pay or move out |
| 4 | Keep communication neutral | Put all messages in writing and avoid threats or admissions | Use a single channel if possible |
| 5 | File with the LTB if unresolved | If the tenant does not pay or leave, file the landlord application after the notice period expires | File only after the notice is complete and valid |
| 6 | Prepare for the hearing | Bring the lease, ledger, notice copy, service proof, photos, repair records, and message history | Organize by date and issue |

## Ontario Tenancy File Checklist

### Core notices and forms
- **N4 notice** for non-payment of rent.
- If damage is significant and you want compensation, keep evidence for a separate landlord claim as needed.
- If the tenant later pays part of the arrears, update the ledger immediately and keep proof.
- Use the exact legal names of all tenants on the lease and notices.

### Evidence to collect
- Signed lease and any renewal or amendment documents.
- A full rent ledger showing:
  - rent amount
  - due dates
  - payments received
  - arrears balance
- Proof of service for every notice sent.
- Photos and videos of the property damage.
- Repair estimates, invoices, and receipts.
- Written communications about rent, repairs, access, or complaints.
- Move-in condition photos, if available, to compare against current damage.
- Witness notes if anyone else saw the damage or condition.

### Timeline considerations
- The tenancy started **2024-09-01**, so it is month-to-month now unless a fixed-term renewal exists.
- For non-payment cases, the notice period must comply with Ontario rules before you can file.
- Do not count informal promises as payment unless money is actually received.
- If the tenant pays all arrears before the termination date in the notice, the eviction path may change.
- Keep every date in a simple chronology:
  - rent due date
  - missed payment date
  - notice served date
  - notice termination date
  - filing date
  - hearing date

### Communication rules
- Keep tone factual, calm, and short.
- Do not argue about blame in the same message as the demand for payment.
- Avoid text messages that could be read as harassment or pressure.
- If repair access is needed, give proper written notice for entry under Ontario rules.

## Neutral Tenant Message Template

Subject: Rent arrears and property condition

Hello [Tenant Name],

This is a written notice that rent for [month 1] and [month 2] remains unpaid. The current arrears total is **CAD 3,700**, plus any additional unpaid amounts that may apply under the lease.

There is also damage to the unit that requires review and documentation. I am collecting records and repair estimates and will keep everything in writing.

Please contact me by [date] to confirm whether you will:
- pay the outstanding rent in full, or
- provide a written plan for resolving the arrears and addressing the damage.

All future communication about this matter should be in writing.

Regards,
[Landlord Name]
[Phone / Email]

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Ontario LTB](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- Action: [Button: Residential Tenancies Act](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- Action: [Button: Tribunals Ontario Forms](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms/)

## Sources

- Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Residential Tenancies Act, 2006: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17
- Tribunals Ontario forms: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms/
